newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan LDP says will try to form four-party bloc.
newsitem.headline: Japan LDP says will try to form four-party bloc.

text.p: Japan's Liberal Democratic Party will try to form a four-party coalition including its two former allies and the fledgling Democratic Party, LDP secretary-general Koichi Kato said after Sunday's election.
"The LDP intends to begin policy negotiations with Sakigake, the Social Democrats and also the Democrats," Kato told reporters.
The conservative LDP, headed by Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto, was projected to fall short of a majority in the 500-seat Lower House, the more powerful of the two chambers in Japan's parliament.

In order to command comfortable majorities in both houses of parliament, the LDP would need the Upper House seats held by the Social Democrats and the new Lower House seats won by the Democratic Party.
In the outgoing coalition government, the LDP was the dominant partner in a three-way alliance with the Social Democratic Party and Sakigake, a small LDP splinter group.
